page: Amazon Web Services f2.6xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, engineered for hardware-accelerated workloads requiring custom FPGA logic. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor delivering 12 physical cores and 24 dedicated vCPUs operating at a 3.4 GHz clock speed, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 256 GB of DDR4 system RAM clocked at 3 GHz, which equates to 10.67 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single Xilinx Virtex UltraScale+ (VU47P) FPGA device equipped with 80 GB of dedicated high-bandwidth memory. Local high-speed storage is bundled in the form of a 940 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 12 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluation reveals a capable CPU subsystem characterized by strong single-core compute performance, ranking in the top 25 percent on stress-ng tests with a score of 2992.08. Multi-core operations align closely with mid-tier enterprise hardware, posting a Geekbench multi-core score of 12705.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 35903.76. Memory throughput is solid, recording 101.18 GB/sec uncached read speeds and 58.21 GB/sec uncached write speeds across large blocks. On artificial intelligence inference metrics evaluated via CPU execution, small 135M language model generation achieved a top-tier 289.78 tokens per second, though throughput degrades considerably on larger models like the 70B variant due to lack of standard tensor-specialized GPU silicon.

From an efficiency standpoint, the f2.6xlarge offers balanced resource density by packaging FPGA hardware, expansive memory, and NVMe scratch space within a single host slice. Workload suitability centers on specialized domain-specific compute, including electronic design automation, real-time video processing pipelines, genomic sequencing, algorithmic trading, and custom hardware accelerator emulation.
description: Amazon Web Services f2.6xlarge is an accelerated computing instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 12 physical cores, 24 dedicated vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, and 256 GB of DDR4 memory. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the platform incorporates a dedicated Xilinx Virtex UltraScale+ (VU47P) FPGA accelerator with 80 GB of high-bandwidth memory, 940 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 12 Gbps baseline network uplink. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU throughput alongside median multi-threaded performance and steady memory bandwidth. While standard CPU-driven execution struggles on dense 70B language models, lightweight inference tasks show solid response rates. The instance delivers a specialized architecture tailored for custom logic acceleration, making it an efficient deployment target for electronic design automation, real-time video transcoding pipelines, genomic search, and financial risk modeling.
